findings.title: View permission grants global group-management access
findings.body: This check treats either `view` or `manage` on the all-groups resource as `canManage()`. Callers of the no-argument `requireManage()`—including top-level group creation—therefore allow an administrator with only view permission to perform management operations across the realm. Require the `manage` scope here; view permission must not grant write access.

findings.title: Group-scoped user search uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: `hasPermission` expects a group ID and resolves it with `findByName`, but this call passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource's database ID). As a result, individual group member-view permissions are not recognized here; line 123 also adds that resource ID to the set consumed as group IDs by user searches. Group-restricted searches can therefore return incomplete or empty pages because filtering happens after pagination without the intended group constraint.
